newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen opening strong after record close.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen opening strong after record close.

text.p: The Dow Industrials index, which closed for the first time above the key 6,000-level on Monday, is expected to shoot even higher on Tuesday, with U.S. technology shares propelled by a strong earnings report from tech bellwether Intel Corp.
The Dow Industrials closed at 6010, up 40.62.

"The question is how far do we go from here," said Peter Cardillo at Westfalia Investments. "The market is going to go higher, but I don't think the Dow can move much beyond the 6,100 level without a normal pullback."
Intel reported third quarter earnings of $1.48 per share, a 40 percent rise from a year ago, and well beyond the Wall Street consensus of $1.25.
Market strategists said they expect U.S. stocks to open stronger, and stay in the plus column for the early part of the day before profit-taking traders move in.
The S&P 500 index December futures were up, indicating in early morning trade that U.S. shares would gain in early action.
Larry Wachtel at Prudential Securities said that the Dow 6000-mark would ultimately have little impact on the direction of stocks.

"The market is ruled by institutional people who run $3, $4, and $5 billion," he said. "I don't think those people are thinking that now I have to spend my money because the Dow hit 6,000. That's nuts."

Wachtel noted the Dow's sharp upswing on Monday was due more to the strength of oil stocks, especially Texaco Inc, Chevron Corp and Exxon Corp, all of which benefitted from a sharp rise in crude oil prices on Monday.
Analysts cited the breadth of the market on Monday, with gainers beating losers by 1209 to 1061 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Cardillo said that after the market moves up by 60 to 70 points, "it will take us into an overbought situation, and a temporary pullback."
Wachtel said he expects a rise of about 20 or 25 points in early trading, then some profit taking.

Tokyo stocks surged on Tuesday, pushed by new record highs on Wall Street as well as speculation that the Liberal Democratic Party may win a majority in the lower house of parliament in Japan's general election on Sunday.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 jumped 400.68, or 1.91 percent, to close at 21,429.93.
The FTSE 100 index gained 21.4 to 4060.1. In London trading, U.S. tech issues led most other U.S. stocks higher on the strong report from Intel.
Shares in Intel were up 7-1/2 to 115 in London, and Texas Instruments, which reported third quarter results of $0.23 vs. $1.48 a year ago. The results beat the mean estimate of $0.20.
Chrysler gained 1/4 to 33 in London after reporting strong third quarter earnings on Monday.
The dollar was standing higher in late Tokyo trade, but had stalled under 112 yen on profit-taking sales.
Although the pound was strong against the dollar and yen, trading was starting to trim some of the gains.
In European trading, the dollar held on to a strong morning rally, and was pushing higher to a fresh 33-month high of 112.26 yen, and a four-month high of 1.5380 marks.
U.S. Treasuries were little changed in Tokyo.

The Wall Street Journal Heard on the Street column reported that experts are watching the "stock market's nosebleed climb with wonder, and, in some cases, worry. But few are willing to predict an end any time soon."
